title: Enhancing Magneto-Optical Activity via Coordination Distortion in Chiral Er4M8 Clusters

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: R-enantiomer of the chiral erbium–cobalt cluster

synthesis.procedure: Lanthanide and cobalt salts were mixed with enantiopure D-HbMe in MeCN; the pH was adjusted with NaOH. The main article gives no reagent quantities or complete procedure.

reagents.name: sodium hydroxide
reagents.amount: 0.4 mL of 1 mol L^-1 aqueous solution (0.4 mmol)

synthesis.temperature: room temperature during stirring; 80 °C during crystallization
synthesis.time: 5 minutes before NaOH addition; 10 minutes after addition; three days at 80 °C
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Sealed in a 20 mL vial and heated to yield purple-red plate-like crystals.

properties.summary: The Co-containing clusters show low-temperature antiferromagnetic coupling and room-temperature paramagnetism. Their absorption, circular dichroism, and magnetic circular dichroism include Co-centered d–d and Er-centered f–f contributions; MCD is independent of enantiomeric handedness.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The cationic Er4Zn8 core is assembled from four cubane-type Er2Zn2 subunits that share Er centers and are linked by μ3-OH bridges into a macrocyclic, square-shaped framework. Acetate links neighboring Er and Zn centers. Each Er center is eight-coordinate, while the Zn centers are five-coordinate; two chloride counterions, two methanol molecules, and three lattice waters accompany the cation.

properties.summary: The bromide-counterion control retains a framework analogous to Er4Zn8. Its Er-centered MCD spectral line shape remains nearly identical, while the dissymmetry response and local Er-site distortion metrics change modestly. The main text does not provide an unambiguous numerical MCD value for this analogue.
